text:
The Lightning are 15-7-2, with 54.6% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and 56% at five on five. Our numbers give them a 94% shot at the playoffs and 43% at the Atlantic. Goals for and against both sit within about two of what the chances predict. This is a good team that is mostly earning it.

So why is everyone writing about them? Nikita Kucherov. The rumor sites have Montreal making a run at him, and Elliotte Friedman was quoted by Montreal Hockey Fanatics on Kent Hughes' potential plan. None of it is more than talk in the headlines we have, and Kucherov is still playing on a line with Jake Guentzel and Brayden Point that has outscored opponents 11-4 at five on five.

The real hit was Conor Geekie, out four to five months after shoulder surgery, per NHL.com. Brandon Hagel and Zemgus Girgensons were expected back against Carolina. The surprise has been the checking line: Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev, 11-5 in goals, the most-used trio on the team. Erik Cernak has eight points in ten, well above the 3.2 expected, and the John Carlson and Charle-Edouard D'Astous pair is 17-6. Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal. What we'd watch is whether the Kucherov noise stays noise; the rest of this roster is doing its job.
headline: Tampa Bay is fine. The headlines are about Kucherov
